title: WHO: COVID-19 deaths were 5.3 million in 2020, 9.4 million in 2021, and 0.9 million in 2023
summary: The causes-of-death sheet gives those three direct-death estimates and the ranks that went with them.
body: WHO's causes-of-death fact sheet says COVID-19 was directly responsible for an estimated 5.3 million deaths in 2020, when it ranked third, and 9.4 million in 2021, when it ranked first. It says deaths directly attributable to COVID-19 fell to 0.9 million in 2023, when it ranked fourteenth, and that 2023 was the first year since 2020 in which COVID-19 was not among the ten leading causes globally. The sheet says "directly." It is not an excess-death total.
